title: Restore a clean, reproducible C++20 build
current_state: A fresh configure succeeds and store_test, parser_test, and executor_test pass. cache_server fails to link because server.cpp and socket.cpp are not in the target. The local tree has no commits, generated artifacts are mixed into it, README.md is empty, warnings apply only to cache_core, and the remote repository contains planning rather than implementation.
body:
Turn the existing partial scaffold into a trustworthy starting point.

Acceptance criteria:
- a fresh out-of-tree configure and full build succeeds, including cache_server
- ctest passes from the fresh build directory
- current server and socket sources are compiled rather than bypassed
- strict warnings apply consistently to project targets
- generated build products are ignored and source, headers, tests, and build configuration are committed
- README contains exact configure, build, test, and run commands

Out of scope:
- CI and sanitizer automation remain in #15

title: Finish and test the move-only Socket wrapper
current_state: Socket already closes its descriptor, deletes copying, transfers ownership in move construction and assignment, and exposes fd(). release/reset behavior, invalid-state tests, and ownership documentation remain.
body:
Finish the RAII boundary already used by socket ownership.

Acceptance criteria:
- destructor closes an owned descriptor exactly once
- copy operations remain deleted
- move construction and assignment transfer ownership safely
- get/fd, release, reset, self-move protection, and invalid state are covered by focused tests
- ownership invariants are documented

Depends on: #1

title: Complete one-client TCP request/response vertical slice
current_state: Server construction creates, configures, binds, and listens, and the event loop accepts nonblocking clients. The path is not buildable or runnable; handle_message calls an undeclared _db.execute API and there is no end-to-end test or documented manual session.
body:
Create the smallest observable server path using the existing listener and client state.

Acceptance criteria:
- socket, bind, listen, and accept failures are handled without descriptor leaks
- one client can connect, send the temporary documented request, and receive PONG
- peer EOF and fatal read/write errors close the client cleanly
- the listening and client descriptors close cleanly on shutdown
- a repeatable manual smoke test is recorded

Depends on: #1 and #2

title: Harden the poll loop for multiple clients and disconnects
current_state: A poll loop and per-client event mask exist, and reverse iteration avoids invalidating later indices during erase. EOF is a TODO, non-EAGAIN read/write errors do not close or propagate, accept errors abort the server, and no concurrent-client integration test exists.
body:
Turn the existing poll skeleton into a correct v1 event loop.

Acceptance criteria:
- multiple clients make progress without blocking one another
- POLLIN, POLLOUT, POLLERR, POLLHUP, and POLLNVAL are handled deliberately
- transient accept/read/write errors do not abort the server
- peer EOF and fatal I/O errors remove exactly the affected connection
- connection state has one clear owner
- an integration test exercises concurrent connect, request, and disconnect behavior

Depends on: #3

title: Integrate per-connection buffers with incremental parsing
current_state: Each Client already owns input and output strings and recv appends bytes. Input is never consumed, incomplete and invalid input cannot be distinguished, and no fragmentation test reaches the TCP boundary.
body:
Connect the incremental parser to the existing per-connection buffers so read boundaries do not define request boundaries.

Acceptance criteria:
- incomplete input remains buffered for the next read
- exactly the consumed prefix is removed after each parsed request
- malformed input yields a bounded error and documented connection policy
- one connection's incomplete or invalid input does not affect another
- tests split representative RESP requests at multiple byte boundaries

Depends on: #4, #6, and #7

title: Implement an incremental binary-safe RESP2 parser
current_state: parseCommand is currently a whitespace tokenizer for SET, GET, and DEL. It has nominal and arity tests but only Valid/Invalid states; it is not RESP, incremental, or binary safe.
body:
Replace the whitespace prototype with the RESP2 subset needed for command requests.

Acceptance criteria:
- parser reports incomplete, valid, or invalid without conflating states
- result reports how many input bytes were consumed
- arrays and bulk strings are supported
- binary bulk-string content, including spaces and NUL bytes, is preserved
- invalid lengths and malformed frames produce bounded errors
- unit tests exercise every byte split for representative requests

Depends on: #1

title: Finish the dispatch boundary and add PING/ECHO
current_state: executeCommand is already separate from Store, and response strings are not embedded in storage. Command-name and arity decisions are still embedded in the whitespace parser, replies are plain text rather than RESP, and PING/ECHO are absent.
body:
Finish separating transport, protocol parsing, dispatch, response encoding, and storage.

Acceptance criteria:
- parser produces a protocol-level argument vector rather than storage-specific command types
- dispatcher owns case-insensitive command lookup and arity validation
- response encoding is independent from Store
- PING and ECHO behavior is implemented with correct RESP replies
- unknown-command and wrong-arity errors are tested

Depends on: #6

title: Finish RESP-safe SET/GET/DEL and add EXISTS
current_state: Store and executeCommand already cover single-key SET, GET, and DEL with focused assertion-based tests. EXISTS, variadic DEL/EXISTS, Redis response types, and protocol-level binary safety remain.
body:
Turn the existing storage prototype into the first Redis-compatible command set.

Acceptance criteria:
- SET and GET preserve binary-safe keys and values
- missing GET returns a RESP null bulk string
- DEL and EXISTS support the documented Redis-compatible multi-key arity
- successful replies use correct RESP types
- command logic has focused unit tests for overwrite, missing keys, multiple keys, and binary content

Depends on: #6 and #7

title: Implement INCR and DECR with integer edge-case tests
body:
Add integer mutation without undefined behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- missing keys follow the documented initial-value behavior
- invalid integer values return an error without mutation
- overflow boundaries are tested and handled
- successful replies use the correct RESP type

Depends on: #8

title: Verify basic redis-cli compatibility
body:
Use redis-cli as an external compatibility check.

Acceptance criteria:
- redis-cli connects to the configured host and port
- all currently supported commands work interactively
- one automated or scripted compatibility smoke test is retained
- unsupported behavior is documented rather than implied

Depends on: #3, #5, #7, and #8

title: Support pipelined requests reliably
current_state: The current server executes the entire accumulated input once and never consumes it, so it cannot safely distinguish or order multiple buffered requests.
body:
Allow multiple complete commands to arrive before replies are drained.

Acceptance criteria:
- all complete requests in an input buffer are dispatched in order
- incomplete trailing input is retained
- replies remain ordered
- per-event work has a documented fairness policy
- integration tests combine pipelining with fragmented input

Depends on: #5 and #7

title: Handle partial writes and slow clients
current_state: Each client already owns an output string and enables POLLOUT. The send loop passes the full buffer size after advancing the pointer, silently continues after fatal send errors, and has no output limit or slow-reader test.
body:
Make output progress independent of send call boundaries.

Acceptance criteria:
- each connection owns queued output plus an unambiguous send offset
- each send length is limited to the remaining unsent bytes
- partial sends retain unsent bytes
- POLLOUT interest is enabled only while useful
- EAGAIN is not treated as a disconnect and fatal errors are handled
- queued output has a documented bound or backpressure policy
- tests exercise a client that drains slowly

Depends on: #4

title: Implement EXPIRE and TTL
body:
Add documented key expiration semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- a monotonic clock is used for elapsed-time decisions
- expiration strategy is documented
- expired keys are not returned by supported commands
- overwrite, delete, missing key, and TTL edge cases are tested
- tests avoid timing flakiness where practical

Depends on: #8

title: Build end-to-end integration test coverage
current_state: Three assertion-based unit-test executables pass for Store, the whitespace parser, and executeCommand. protocol_test.cpp is empty and no test starts the server or uses the TCP boundary.
body:
Build reusable tests for the running server through its TCP boundary, extending coverage alongside features.

Acceptance criteria:
- test harness starts and stops the server deterministically
- raw RESP requests and replies are validated
- fragmented requests, pipelining, disconnects, concurrent clients, and slow readers are covered as their issues land
- failures leave no orphan server process
- integration tests run through CTest

Can start after: #3

title: Run strict warnings, ASan, and UBSan in CI
current_state: Only cache_core has -Wall -Wextra -pedantic. There is no CI workflow, sanitizer configuration, or documented local sanitizer command.
body:
Make compiler and runtime checks routine after the reproducible local build exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- warning-clean builds are required for all project code
- ASan and UBSan test jobs run in CI
- sanitizer failures fail the workflow
- local reproduction commands are documented
- TSan remains deferred unless concurrency is introduced

Depends on: #1; complete after the integration harness in #14 is available

title: Create a reproducible baseline benchmark
body:
Measure the stable poll implementation before optimizing it.

Acceptance criteria:
- workload, client count, payload, hardware, and build mode are recorded
- warmup and multiple measured runs are used
- throughput plus median and tail latency are reported when the tool supports them
- limitations and measurement noise are stated
- no superiority claim is made without a valid comparison

Entry gate: core compatibility, I/O correctness, expiration, integration tests, and sanitizer CI are complete

title: Document architecture, commands, and known limitations
current_state: The implementation-tree README is empty. The remote README and roadmap describe intended scope but not build/run steps, current architecture, supported behavior, or verified limitations.
body:
Keep user and architecture documentation current, then finish the interview-ready presentation after the benchmark.

Acceptance criteria:
- README has build, test, sanitizer, and run instructions
- architecture explains ownership, event loop, parsing, storage, and expiration
- supported-command table states exact behavior
- example redis-cli session is included
- benchmark method and results are linked
- known limitations are explicit

Can start after: #1; final completion follows #16

title: Compare epoll only after the poll baseline is stable
body:
This is deliberately post-v1 and must not pull focus from correctness.

Entry criteria:
- fragmented reads, pipelining, partial writes, disconnects, and slow clients are tested
- sanitizer CI is green
- baseline benchmark is reproducible
- v1 documentation is complete

Acceptance criteria:
- existing connection and parsing interfaces are preserved where practical
- the full test suite passes against epoll
- the same benchmark compares poll and epoll
- results are explained without overclaiming

Depends on: #16 and #17
